To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Dynamic contrast perfusion MRI analysis represents a complementary tool for identifying vasmocularity characteristics of tumor tissues in local advanced rectum cancer.
dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI is a useful tool to evaluate tumor vascularity and to predict the treatment response in rectal cancer.

dynamic perfusion MRI is a promising tool in the evaluation of tumor response to chemoradiation in local advanced rect cancer, and that the combination of different perfusion parameters is able to differentiate between responders and non responders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the evaluation of the potential role of perfusion-MRI as a non-invasive tool to assess the treatment response of rectal cancer after chemo-radiotherapy.
a new diagnostic tool for the prediction of complete response in patients with local-advanced rectal cancer, based on perfusion MRI parameters.
the use of perfusion parameters as a predictor of response to neoadjuvant chemoradiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
perfusion MRI may represent a valuable tool for the prediction of response to chemoradiation in patients with local rectal cancer.
dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI is a useful tool for the prediction of complete response after chemo-radiotherapy in local advanced rectum carcinoma.
dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI is not yet a standard tool for predicting tumor response to neoadjuvant chemoradiation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of dynamic perfusion MRI in the evaluation of rectal cancer is a promising method to assess the response of the tumor tissue to neoadjuvant treatment, and to predict the histopathologic tumor regression grade (Mandard classification).
dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI parameters are significantly different between responders and nonresponders, with a better performance of the AUC in predicting tumor response.
perfusion parameters of tumor tissue at MR2 could represent an early indicator of response to chemoradiation treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the evaluation of tumor response to chemonoradiation therapy can be obtained by using perfusion MRI parameters, with a good correlation with histopathologic findings, in comparison to the current standard of care.

perfusion parameters, particularly RAE, RVE, RLE and AUC, can be useful for predicting tumor regression and may be considered as a reliable method for predicting complete tumor regression in patients with local-advanced rectal cancer.

the use of DCE-MRI in combination with other imaging modalities, such as diffusion-weighted imaging, may provide an additional value to the evaluation of tumor treatment response in rectal cancer patients.
